Guidance/Concept: PM must establish, capture, record, approve, and maintain the project's software requirements (including COTS/GOTS/MOTS/OSS/reused components) as part of the technical specification.
Our Interpretation: This is a directive that the PM run the requirements-management process (elicit, document, approve, maintain); it describes an activity performed on the requirement set, not a quality test of one requirement sentence.
Questions: Could be read as MULTIPLE since the object being maintained is the requirement set as a whole, but the shall-verb structure targets PM activity, so we kept it PROCESS.

Guidance/Concept: PM must analyze software requirements, deriving and flowing them down from systems-engineering requirements, safety/reliability analyses, and hardware specs/design.
Our Interpretation: The obligation is on the PM to perform an analysis activity across the requirement set's sources; it is not a per-sentence check of one requirement.
Questions: One could argue each derived requirement's traceability to its source is an individual/SET concern, but the shall-clause mandates the analysis activity itself, not a quality criterion.

Guidance/Concept: PM must ensure the software requirements documentation includes safety-related constraints, controls, mitigations, and assumptions spanning hardware, operator, and software.
Our Interpretation: The shall-clause is a PM action (include content), but what is being evaluated -- whether the documentation set as a whole contains the required safety content -- is naturally checked against the full SRS, so we call this PROCESS + SET.

Guidance/Concept: PM must track and manage changes made to the software requirements.
Our Interpretation: Classic change-management activity; not evaluable from any single requirement sentence.

Guidance/Concept: PM must identify inconsistencies among requirements, project plans, and software products, and drive corrective actions to closure.
Our Interpretation: The underlying concept being checked -- mutual consistency across requirements/plans/products -- is a SET-level property, but the shall-clause is a PM corrective-action process, so PROCESS + SET.

Guidance/Concept: PM must validate the requirements to confirm the resulting software will perform as intended in the customer's operating environment.
Our Interpretation: Validation here is an activity the PM performs against the whole software system; the shall-clause obligates the PM to run this process.
Questions: Validating 'the software' against the requirement set could be read as a SET-level check (MULTIPLE); we kept PROCESS because the requirement's locus of control is the PM's validation activity, not a documented SET attribute.

Guidance/Concept: PM must turn the software requirements into a documented software architecture.
Our Interpretation: Directs an engineering activity (architecture design) performed by/for the PM.

Guidance/Concept: PM must conduct a software architecture review for Category 1 & 2 Class A/B projects.
Our Interpretation: A scheduled review activity mandated of the PM.

Guidance/Concept: PM must develop, record, and maintain a software design, based on the architecture, detailed enough to code/compile/test.
Our Interpretation: Design-development activity performed by the PM/team.

Guidance/Concept: PM must implement the software design as code.
Our Interpretation: Implementation activity; a process step, not a requirement-quality check.

Guidance/Concept: PM must select, define, and follow coding methods, standards, and criteria.
Our Interpretation: Establishing and enforcing coding standards is a process control.

Guidance/Concept: PM must use static analysis tools during development/testing to catch defects, security issues, coverage gaps, and complexity.
Our Interpretation: Tooling/process mandate for the development activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must unit test the software code.
Our Interpretation: Testing activity performed by the PM/team.

Guidance/Concept: PM must ensure unit test results are repeatable.
Our Interpretation: Quality assurance of the test process itself.

Guidance/Concept: PM must produce a software version description for each release.
Our Interpretation: Documentation/release-management activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must validate and accredit the software tools used to develop/maintain the software.
Our Interpretation: Tool-qualification process.

Guidance/Concept: PM must establish and maintain certain test-related plans/procedures (clause text is truncated in the source CSV).
Our Interpretation: Planning/maintenance activity, consistent with the verb pattern of this section.
Questions: Row text is truncated in the source CSV ('shall establish and maintain:'), so the exact scope is unclear; classification is based on the verb pattern common to this section.

Guidance/Concept: PM must test the software against its requirements.
Our Interpretation: Verification activity; the PM runs the tests, so the obligation is process-level even though the requirement set is the test basis.
Questions: Could be seen as MULTIPLE since it directly references testing against 'its requirements' (the SET), but we treated the core obligation as the testing process.

Guidance/Concept: PM must place software items under configuration management before testing begins.
Our Interpretation: Configuration-management process step.

Guidance/Concept: PM must evaluate test results and document that evaluation.
Our Interpretation: Test-evaluation/reporting activity.

Guidance/Concept: For flight software/equipment, PM must use validated and accredited models, simulations, and analysis tools for qualification.
Our Interpretation: Tool-qualification/process control specific to flight projects.

Guidance/Concept: PM must keep the software test/verification plans and procedures consistent with the software requirements.
Our Interpretation: Maintaining these plan documents is a PM process activity; the target of consistency (the requirement set) is a SET concept, but the obligation itself is to perform an update/maintenance action.
Questions: Consistency-with-requirements could support MULTIPLE; flagging for team discussion.

Guidance/Concept: PM must validate the software system on the actual target platform or a high-fidelity simulation.
Our Interpretation: System validation activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must ensure code-coverage measurements are selected, implemented, tracked, recorded, and reported.
Our Interpretation: Metrics-process mandate.

Guidance/Concept: PM must verify that code coverage is measured through analysis of actual test-execution results.
Our Interpretation: Verification/measurement process.

Guidance/Concept: PM must plan and conduct regression testing to confirm no defects or security vulnerabilities were introduced into previously tested software.
Our Interpretation: Testing-process activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must verify, through test, the specific software requirements that trace to a hazard, cause, or mitigation technique.
Our Interpretation: The verification activity is process-driven (the PM runs the tests), but it is explicitly scoped to individual hazard-traced requirements, so this is PROCESS + INDIVIDUAL.

Guidance/Concept: PM must develop acceptance tests for any loaded or uplinked data, rules, or code that affects software/system behavior.
Our Interpretation: Test-development activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must test embedded COTS/GOTS/MOTS/OSS/reused components to the same rigor as custom-developed components.
Our Interpretation: Testing-standard/process mandate.

Guidance/Concept: PM must plan and carry out software operations, maintenance, and retirement activities.
Our Interpretation: Life-cycle-phase planning activity.

Guidance/Concept: PM must complete and deliver the software product to the customer along with appropriate records (e.g., as-built records) supporting operations and maintenance.
Our Interpretation: Delivery/documentation process.

Guidance/Concept: Before delivery, PM must confirm all requirements for that delivery have been met or dispositioned, approved changes implemented, and required defects resolved.
Our Interpretation: The verification act is a PM process step, but its content is explicitly a SET-level completeness check across 'all software requirements identified for this delivery', so PROCESS + SET.

Guidance/Concept: PM must maintain the software per the standards/processes for its applicable software classification throughout the maintenance phase.
Our Interpretation: Maintenance-process compliance.

Guidance/Concept: PM must identify which records/tools to archive, where, and how they will be accessed for retirement/disposal.
Our Interpretation: Archival/retirement planning activity.

Guidance/Concept: The SRS introduction section should establish the purpose/scope of the requirements and introduce the system being built.
Our Interpretation: This describes what a whole document section should contain/accomplish across the entire SRS, not a property of any one requirement sentence.

Guidance/Concept: Recommends organizing requirements by CSCI (for planning, staffing, sizing) and co-locating each requirement's rationale nearby.
Our Interpretation: Concerns how the whole requirement set/document is organized.

Guidance/Concept: Describes the SRS section that documents the method (test/analysis/inspection/demonstration) used to verify or validate each requirement.
Our Interpretation: It is a document-structure topic (a section of the SRS -- SET), but the content it prescribes -- one verification method per requirement -- is assessed at the level of each individual requirement, so PROCESS/SET is not enough on its own; we used INDIVIDUAL + SET.

Guidance/Concept: Recommends including rationale that explains why each requirement exists and its importance, placed alongside the requirement it supports.
Our Interpretation: Rationale is authored and attached per individual requirement (INDIVIDUAL) but is also framed as a standard SRS section/practice (SET).

Guidance/Concept: Notes that other requirements or supporting information necessary to build the software should also be captured/documented in the SRS.
Our Interpretation: About what content the overall SRS should include.

Guidance/Concept: Defines functional requirements as the specific user-facing behaviors/functions/features the system must perform.
Our Interpretation: This is a definitional test you apply to a single requirement sentence to decide whether it is functional.

Guidance/Concept: Defines non-functional requirements (NFRs) as the quality attributes, performance constraints, and operational characteristics governing how functions are delivered, versus what the system does.
Our Interpretation: Applied per requirement sentence to classify its type.

Guidance/Concept: Defines interface requirements as those describing how the software interacts with other systems, hardware, users, or components, at the system's boundaries.
Our Interpretation: Applied per requirement sentence to classify its type.

Guidance/Concept: A well-written requirement is clear and unambiguous, avoiding subjective terms and stating exactly what is required.
Our Interpretation: Directly checkable by reading one requirement sentence in isolation.

Guidance/Concept: A well-written requirement must be specific enough to be verified against a defined, objective success criterion.
Our Interpretation: Checkable from a single requirement sentence.

Guidance/Concept: A well-written requirement links to a user need, goal, use case, or parent requirement, and carries a unique identifier.
Our Interpretation: Whether a given requirement carries an ID/parent-link can be checked by looking at that one requirement.
Questions: Borderline: fully verifying traceability (that the cited parent/link actually exists and is valid) is really a SET-level check; we classified INDIVIDUAL because the row describes the requirement carrying the attribute, not validating the whole chain.

Guidance/Concept: A well-written requirement covers all expected inputs, outputs, and scenarios relevant to the behavior it specifies, with no missing conditions.
Our Interpretation: Assessable from the single requirement's own scope statement.

Guidance/Concept: Derived/decomposed requirements should remain testable and measurable so conformance can be objectively evaluated.
Our Interpretation: Applied to each individual (derived/decomposed) requirement sentence.

Guidance/Concept: The SRS should identify which functions are critical versus optional so effort and risk can be managed accordingly.
Our Interpretation: Despite being tagged 'characteristic' like the individual-quality rows, this guidance explicitly talks about the SRS ranking functions relative to each other -- you cannot tell if one requirement is 'prioritized' by reading it alone; you need the whole set to know its relative priority. We therefore classified this SET rather than INDIVIDUAL.
Questions: This departs from the pattern of the other 'characteristic' rows and from the team's working assumption that all six characteristic rows map to INDIVIDUAL; flagging for a second opinion, since 'Prioritized' could also be argued as PROCESS (a risk-management activity).

Guidance/Concept: Defines two requirement types: Decomposed requirements are lower-level, more detailed requirements produced by breaking down a higher-level functional/non-functional requirement (e.g. REQ-001.1); Derived requirements instead originate from design/implementation decisions rather than directly from a stakeholder need.
Our Interpretation: Decomposed-ness requires comparing a requirement to its parent (a SET-level relationship you cannot see from one requirement sentence alone); derived-ness describes where a requirement came from relative to a design/implementation decision, which is also not verifiable from the requirement text in isolation. Both halves resist a pure INDIVIDUAL classification, so we keep this MULTIPLE (INDIVIDUAL label applied to a requirement + a SET/PROCESS-level origin question).

Guidance/Concept: Explains states as system situations with defined conditions, and calls for specifying system behavior in each state and its transitions.
Our Interpretation: A single requirement can describe one state's behavior (INDIVIDUAL), but a complete state model spans multiple related requirements describing all states and transitions together (SET).

Guidance/Concept: Describes software safety requirements as defining the conditions/constraints/behaviors needed to avoid or mitigate hazards, pointing to SWE-134 for the specific safety items that must be addressed.
Our Interpretation: The content a safety requirement must contain is an individual-requirement concern (INDIVIDUAL), but it also references SWE-134's PM-level implementation obligation (PROCESS).

Guidance/Concept: Non-functional/performance requirements should state precise, measurable metrics (e.g., response time, throughput, latency) with the conditions/load they apply under, rather than vague terms.
Our Interpretation: This is a per-sentence writing-quality check, the same kind of test as 'Specific'/'Measurable'.

Guidance/Concept: Restates that the PM shall establish/capture/record/approve/maintain software requirements, calling it the foundational reference for everything the SRS documents.
Our Interpretation: The underlying shall-clause is a PM process action (PROCESS), but SWEHB explicitly frames it as the basis for the whole SRS's content, so we classified this SWEHB row PROCESS + SET (distinct from the NPR row for the same SWE-050, which we kept as plain PROCESS since it lacks that SRS-content framing).
Questions: Team should confirm whether the NPR-row and SWEHB-row versions of the same underlying SWE-xxx requirement must always be classified identically; we treated each CSV row independently based on its own phrasing.

Guidance/Concept: Notes the PM's requirements-analysis obligation and that SWEHB cites it alongside SWE-050 for requirements decomposition/analysis discussions.
Our Interpretation: Same PM-driven analysis activity as the NPR row for SWE-051.

Guidance/Concept: Safety requirements should be marked/tagged as such and carry a unique identifier so they can be traced and their impacts assessed through development and operations.
Our Interpretation: Whether one requirement carries the safety tag/ID is checkable on that single requirement, consistent with how we classified the 'Traceable' row above.

Guidance/Concept: Points to SWE-053 for managing requirement changes and to another topic for baselining/updating the SRS ahead of milestone reviews.
Our Interpretation: Change-management/baselining is a PM process activity.

Guidance/Concept: Lists specific safety items the PM shall implement in the software when the project has safety- or mission-critical software.
Our Interpretation: The shall-clause is a PM implementation obligation (PROCESS), but the 'items' being implemented are effectively content requirements for individual safety-critical design requirements (INDIVIDUAL).

Guidance/Concept: Requirements-volatility data is tracked in the Software Metrics Report, and this topic also introduces detailed guidance on the SRS's minimum recommended content.
Our Interpretation: Tracking/reporting metrics is a PM process activity (PROCESS), while volatility itself and 'minimum recommended content' describe properties of the requirement set/SRS as a whole (SET).
